desc: A carved stone statue. The one subject where having no texture and no vertex colour hurts least.
source_prompt: a single carved stone statue of a standing robed figure on a square plinth, arms held close to the body, deep drapery folds, head facing forward, the whole statue and plinth inside the frame with margin on all sides, three-quarter view, flat mid-grey seamless background, even frontal light, no cast shadow, no gallery, no other statues
output: untextured GLB mesh, POSITION attribute only, ~525k tris, ~8.5 MB, 19.5 s
usable_for: set dressing once a stone material is assigned, blockout, sculpt base, 3D-print base
not_usable_for: direct game import - still needs retopology and UVs if it must carry a detailed material
note: The honest sweet spot of this whole library. Every other preset ships a mesh that looks wrong until it is textured; a statue assigned one flat grey stone material in Blender reads as finished, because real carved stone is a single uniform material with no pattern. Arms are specified close to the body on purpose - outstretched thin limbs are lost by the iso-surface. Drapery folds survive because they are volume, not texture.
